classification.difficultyReason: Supplied parts guide an equal-angle proof, calculation of lengths using exact 30° ratios, and rationalisation of the resulting tangent ratio.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle PRS with Q between P and R, internal segment QS, and a right-angle marker at R.
spec.mathematics: P, Q and R are collinear in that order. SR is perpendicular to PR. Angle SPR is 15 degrees and angle SQR is 30 degrees. Coordinates derive these relationships; no numerical side lengths are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied vertex labels, angle values and right-angle marker are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQS&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\&=150^{\circ}\\\angle PSQ&=180^{\circ}-150^{\circ}-15^{\circ}\\&=15^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The first calculation uses angles on a straight line. Since $\angle PSQ=\angle QPS$, the opposite sides are equal. Hence $PQ=QS$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that the length of $SR$ is 1 unit, write the lengths of $QR$, $QS$, and $PQ$.

answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $QRS$,
$$\begin{align*}\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{SR}{QS}\\\frac12&=\frac1{QS}\\QS&=2\end{align*}$$
By part a, $PQ=QS=2$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan30^{\circ}&=\frac{SR}{QR}\\\frac1{\sqrt3}&=\frac1{QR}\\QR&=\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Thus $QR=\sqrt3$ units and $QS=PQ=2$ units.
